transitions.observation: Evening office to a bright reception. 'A later morning:' gives the time jump. A tidy desk with a monitor and no register stack replaces the page 1 paperwork. Meera is in the same blue kurta and braid.

Second check-in route. Priya outside on the street, with the clinic's glass door, waiting chairs and the reception TV visible behind her, so she is clearly heading to the same clinic. 'Some check in ahead' contrasts with the front desk.

Third route. Inside the glass entrance, Ravi scans the QR stand. The background shows Meera at the desk, Raman at the counter and a ponytailed woman seated, which ties the three routes to the same morning. The caption introduces Ravi by name.
Close-up of the same phone (dark case) and wristwatch. The scan leads straight into the form with a consent tick. Cause and effect are clear.

A wide shot of the waiting area. Raman (stick, glasses), Priya (ponytail, coral kurti) and Ravi (green shirt, phone in hand, bag on his lap) sit left to right under the TV listing three slots. All three routes end in one queue.

Page turn, same waiting area. Ravi stands with his bag back on his shoulder and his phone going into his pocket. The TV shows 'NOW · A-12' and the chairs at his left are empty. 'Soon, his slot comes up.' confirms that A-12 is his, which page 3 only implied by the seating order.

This is acceptable and intended: the seating suggests A-12, and 04-1 confirms it on the next page, which the reader also noted. (3) The 03-2 caption touches the borders. This is placement style and it covers nothing. The reader found no covered faces or hands, and I confirm that, including the tight 03-2 margin beside Priya's face. Nothing unresolved remains.
